title: Microwave interior and exterior care
audience: Cleaners who service shared and staff microwaves in break rooms, offices and short-stay properties.
learningOutcomes: Describe the common microwave types and finishes you will meet on site.
Clean the interior from the top down, removing the turntable or cook tray for separate washing.
Clean the exterior and controls without letting liquid reach the vents or the control panel.

instruction.heading: Know what you are cleaning
instruction.body: Microwaves in workplaces come as over-the-range units, built-in units and countertop units. Their finishes are usually painted enamel or polished steel. The finish sets which cloth and cleaner you use: enamel tolerates a general cleaner well, while stainless steel should be wiped along the grain and never scoured. Before you start, look for vents, a control panel and any removable tray. Those features tell you where liquid must not go and what needs to be taken out.

instruction.heading: Interior: top down, then remove and wash the tray
instruction.body: Lift out the turntable or cook tray first and clean it on its own, resting it on paper towel while you work. Then apply cleaner to a cloth or spray the interior surfaces directly, and wipe from the ceiling down the sides and back. Finish with the cavity floor, collecting loose crumbs and tipping them into the bin so they do not drop onto the tray you have just cleaned. Clean the interior of the door and the door seal. For baked-on spots, apply product, let it sit briefly to soften, then loosen and wipe. Do not force a scraper against the interior lining.

instruction.heading: Exterior, controls and returning it to use
instruction.body: Use a cloth dampened with cleaner, not a soaked one, on the control buttons, the door handle and the door frame. Spray the cloth, never the controls or the vents. Wipe the exterior of the body and the top, then dry the surfaces that have been wet. Replace the tray in its correct position before the unit is switched on. Check the interior has no smell of cleaner, because a residue can taint food that is heated afterwards.

procedure: Put on gloves and check the unit is switched off and unplugged or isolated if the site rules require it.
Lift out the turntable or cook tray and clean it separately, resting it on paper towel.
Spray the cloth, not the unit, and wipe the ceiling, then the sides and the rear of the interior.
Collect loose crumbs from the cavity floor and tip them into the bin.
Wipe the interior of the door and the door seal.
Soften baked-on spots by applying product, waiting briefly, then working them loose and wiping.
Clean the keypad, handle and frame using a damp cloth.
Wipe the exterior and dry any wet surfaces.
Return the tray to its position and check the interior for residue before the unit is used.

workedExamples.situation: A shared microwave in a break room has a sticky control panel and a crust of spilled food on the floor of the cavity. The cleaner sprays the control panel directly.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the mistake, and how should the panel be cleaned?
workedExamples.reasoning: Spraying directly onto the control panel can drive liquid into the switches and openings. Spray a cloth and wipe the panel gently instead. The crust in the cavity should be sprayed, allowed to dwell, then loosened and wiped with a cloth.

workedExamples.situation: A stainless steel microwave shows swirl marks after a cleaner has used a coarse scourer on the outside.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner do next time?
workedExamples.reasoning: Use a soft cloth dampened with a mild cleaner and wipe along the grain of the steel. Avoid scourers on stainless finishes because they leave marks that show up in the light.

equipmentAndPpe: Colour-coded microfiber cloths and paper towel.
Approved general cleaner suitable for the finish, with its label and safety data sheet available.
Soft brush for corners and seals.
Bin and a small plastic scraper or spatula for crumbs that will not wipe away, used with care.
Stainless steel polish, only where the site product list allows it.

commonErrors.error: Spraying the control panel or the vents directly.
commonErrors.prevention: Spray the cloth and wipe the controls gently. Keep liquid away from openings.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the turntable in place, so the floor under it is missed.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the tray first, clean it, and then clean under and around where it sat.

commonErrors.error: Using a coarse scourer on a stainless finish.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a soft cloth and a mild cleaner, wiping along the grain.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Do not open the unit, remove panels, or work on its electrical parts. Clean only the accessible interior and exterior.
Keep liquid away from vents, openings and the control panel. Do not use the unit until it is dry inside.
Do not use the microwave to heat anything while the cleaning product is still present. Check the interior for residue first.

qualityStandard: The interior is clean from ceiling to floor, with no crumbs or residue.
The door, door seal and frame are clean.
The control buttons are clean and dry, with no liquid in them.
The stainless steel exterior is streak free and has no new marks.
The tray is clean and sitting in its correct position.
No cleaner smell is present when the unit is next used.
documentationEvidence: Job record showing the microwave was cleaned, with the date and time.
Note of any damaged control, seal or tray for repair.
Note of any unit that will not switch on after cleaning, so the supervisor can check it.
summary: Identify the finish and any vents or controls before you start.
Remove and wash the tray, then clean the interior from the top down.
Spray the cloth, never the controls or vents.
Check for residue before the unit is used again.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should the control panel of a microwave be cleaned?
options: Spray the panel directly until the surface is wet and let it run down into the vents
Spray a cloth and wipe gently, keeping liquid away from the controls and vents
Soak the panel in a bucket of cleaner and then rinse it under the tap

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is the cook tray removed before the interior is cleaned?
options: Because the tray must be replaced with a new one each time from the supplier
So that the microwave can be switched on while cleaning and the tray stays in place
So that the tray can be washed separately and the floor beneath it can be cleaned

knowledgeChecks.question: A stainless steel microwave is being cleaned. Which approach is correct?
options: Use a soft cloth dampened with a mild cleaner and wipe along the grain
Use a coarse scourer in rotating strokes to lift the soil
Use oven cleaner so the finish shines immediately on the whole front
